correctness.rationale: For q even, R=F_2 I+N is a finite ring because the strictly upper triangular algebra N is closed and nilpotent. Its elements with zero diagonal are nilpotent nonunits, while every I+X is invertible by a finite geometric series, so its unit group is exactly UT_n(q). For n=2 the group is C_p^f, and the published odd-order classification gives the exact Mersenne-prime condition. For n>=3 and p odd, the explicit elementary matrices I+E_12 and I+E_23 do not commute, while every realizable finite odd-primary p-group is elementary abelian. The packaged checker independently verifies the constructive half in several finite fields.

originality.rationale: The 2024 primary paper initiates Fuchs-problem analysis for linear groups but its full searchable text has no unitriangular-family theorem. The 2019 odd-primary classification supplies the obstruction but does not single out or classify UT_n(q). The 2019/2020 2-group work shows that realizability of 2-groups is subtle and likewise contains no unitriangular discussion in the inspected full text. The accepted statement combines these directions with a direct characteristic-two construction to give a complete iff classification for a classical linear family.

value.rationale: Unitriangular groups are a standard infinite family of finite nilpotent linear groups, while Fuchs realizability is known to be delicate even for 2-groups. The theorem gives a complete parameter classification rather than isolated examples, identifies an exact odd-characteristic boundary, and supplies an explicit minimal-size local realizing ring for every even field. It therefore adds a natural classical family to the realizability landscape studied by the motivating linear-groups paper.
